text:
Erin Jacobs: Quick heads-up: starting an owner-clarity sweep for KMS keys + admin entitlements across prod and staging. Goal: reduce ownerless/admin bindings by ~30% this sprint. Anyone blocking?
Samir Patel: Thanks — sounds good. Can you drop the query/scan you used? I can run it against analytics and svcacct inventories.
oncall-bot: scheduled-audit-bot: automated job finished 2026-03-05T02:00Z — found 42 ownerless keys in prod, 9 in staging.
Erin Jacobs: Copy. I'll paste the basic gcloud/sql snippets in a sec. Plan idea: map owner claims, attempt outreach (48h), then do a canary prune (dev -> staging -> prod) with rollback tags.
Jia Chen: 42 matches our estimate. Canary-prune is the right call. We should standardize the outreach template and include instructions for escalations.
Kyle (SRE): Also watch for service accounts with inline grants or workload identities that won't show up in project-iam scans. Update runbook to check Cloud Audit Logs for recent key usage before pruning.
Samir Patel: Query I ran (simplified):
```sql
SELECT key_name, project_id, owner_email
FROM kms_key_owners
WHERE owner_email IS NULL OR owner_email = ''
ORDER BY project_id;
```
And the gcloud one-liner to enumerate bindings:
```bash
gcloud kms keys list --location global --project=$PROJECT 
  --format="csv(name,primaryVersion.createTime)"
# then check IAM: gcloud projects get-iam-policy $PROJECT --format=json
```
Samir Patel: My plan: add `--dry-run` output for review, then `--tag=pre-prune` on keys we intend to touch so we can auto-skip if usage spikes.
Erin Jacobs: Action items: 1) @Samir — run dry-run canary in dev by EOD Tue and post results here. 2) @Jia — draft outreach template + exception request flow. 3) @Kyle — update runbook with audit-log checklist and rollback steps. 4) I'll open a JIRA with rollout timeline and acceptance criteria.
Jia Chen: Will do. Suggest adding an example audit-log snippet to the template showing 'cryptoKeyVersions.use' entries and how to interpret timestamps.
Samir Patel: I'll include `--dry-run > dryrun.json` and a small script snippet for tag/untag:
```bash
# dry run
./scripts/kms-owner-sweep.sh --project dev --dry-run > dryrun.json
# tag example
./scripts/kms-tag.sh --key projects/x/locations/global/keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/key --add tag:pre-prune
```
Kyle (SRE): Good. Also add monitoring alert: if any pruned key shows usage in the next 48h, auto-trigger a rollback playbook.
Erin Jacobs: Great. Once Samir posts dry-run, we'll review and decide staging window. I'll ping product-security for visibility.
Samir Patel: Posted dryrun.json to the thread and uploaded to /internal/sec/kms-audits/dev/dryrun.json. It's a short list (5 keys) for dev. No recent crypto operations in the last 30d.
Jia Chen: Draft outreach uploaded: /internal/sec/templates/kms-owner-outreach.md — includes exception form, SLA for responses (48h), and escalation to oncall if no reply.
Kyle (SRE): Runbook PR opened: https://git.internal/repo/ops/runbooks/kms-owner-prune.md — added audit-log checks and rollback steps.
Erin Jacobs: Nice. Next checkpoint: review dev dry-run at 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC, then schedule staging window. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: :thumbsup:
Jia Chen: :raised_hands:
Kyle (SRE): :eyes:
